title: Mathematics
identity: Rigorous analysis, probability, geometry, topology and algebra, taught the way mathematicians work: definitions first, examples and non-examples, theorems with their hypotheses in view, and proofs written out in full. Nothing here is a service course; the subject is studied for its own sake, from undergraduate foundations to graduate material.
conventions: ℕ starts at 1 unless a course says otherwise; ℝ and ℂ are the real and complex fields.
Norms are written ‖·‖ with a subscript naming the space or the exponent; inner products are ⟨·,·⟩, linear in the first argument.
A theorem is stated with all its hypotheses before any proof begins; a counterexample is given whenever a hypothesis is dropped.
Proofs end with a short remark on which hypothesis did the work.
